_comment: Precursor playbook. Each scenario lists observable warning signs seen before past strikes and crises, with weights (score = sum of lit weights, max 100). 'why' explains the historical basis. Scores measure how many warning signs are showing, not a probability.

scenarios.name: Local emergency in SA (bushfire, heat, power)
scenarios.sa_impact: Direct: bushfires, heatwaves and power cuts are the emergencies most likely to affect the family. In the 2016 statewide blackout, power, phones, traffic lights and fuel pumps failed together.
scenarios.why: The worst local days stack up: extreme fire danger, a heatwave pushing power demand, a tight grid, and storms or fires damaging lines. AEMO warns of supply shortfalls hours to a day ahead; the CFS and Bureau issue ratings and warnings a day or more ahead.

indicators.name: CFS Emergency Warning in SA
CFS Watch and Act in SA
Extreme or Catastrophic fire danger near Adelaide
Total fire ban for Adelaide or the Hills
Bureau severe weather or heatwave warning for SA
Tight power supply in SA (AEMO lack of reserve, level 2+)
Phone / internet carrier outage
Fire, flood or storm road closures in SA
Three or more Adelaide emergency departments 'very busy'
Reports of widespread power outages in SA
SA Water supply cut or water-quality notice reported
Adelaide reservoirs below 30% (any)
Sudden fall in SA electricity demand (possible large blackout)

scenarios.name: Middle East war & Gulf shipping
scenarios.sa_impact: Fuel: Australia imports most of its fuel, much of it refined from Gulf crude in Asia. Shipping attacks or a Hormuz closure push up prices within days and can cause local shortages.
scenarios.why: Before the 2024-25 Israel-Iran exchanges and US strikes, watchers saw US tanker surges toward Europe and the Gulf, embassy departure orders, regional GPS jamming, airspace closures and oil price jumps, often 1-3 days ahead.

indicators.name: Air-refuelling tanker surge
Unusual military air activity over the region
GPS jamming spike (Gulf / Israel)
Internet blackout in Iran or Israel
New US embassy departure order in the region
Airspace closures reported (Iran / Israel / Gulf)
Military navigation warnings (Gulf / Red Sea)
Brent oil up 4%+ in a day
Spy-satellite passes converging on Iran / Israel
US defence stocks outperforming (5 days)
Mass casualty declarations in the region
Vessels loitering over Red Sea cables
Ship traffic through Hormuz down sharply
Ship traffic through Bab el-Mandeb down sharply
Forecast markets jump on Iran conflict

scenarios.name: Taiwan Strait / South China Sea crisis
scenarios.sa_impact: Trade and fuel: most of Australia's refined fuel and many goods pass the South China Sea. A blockade would disrupt fuel, medicines and electronics within weeks; Australian forces could be drawn in.
scenarios.why: China's large drills around Taiwan (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025) were announced through maritime navigation warnings, with GPS interference and coastguard surges; any real operation would be expected to add mobilisation reports and internet disruption.

indicators.name: Missile / live-fire navigation warnings near Taiwan
GPS jamming over the Taiwan Strait
Internet disruption in Taiwan
Unusual military air activity near Taiwan
Mobilisation / reservist reports (China or Taiwan)
Military airlift or RAAF surge
New US embassy departure order (Taiwan / China)
Spy-satellite passes converging on Taiwan
Chinese war-preparation signalling
Military blood drives / field hospitals (China / Taiwan)
Defence stocks outperforming (US / Australia)
Chinese state hacking reports (Volt / Salt Typhoon)
Chinese / HK vessels loitering over Taiwan's cables
Taiwan undersea cable damage reported
Ship traffic through Taiwan / Luzon Strait down sharply
Forecast markets jump on China-Taiwan conflict

scenarios.name: Korean Peninsula conflict
scenarios.sa_impact: Indirect: market shock, Australian citizens in Korea and Japan, and US-allied commitments. Little direct physical risk to SA.
scenarios.why: North Korean missile launches are often preceded by navigation warnings; South Korea and Japan report GPS jamming from the North during tense periods.

indicators.name: Missile navigation warnings (Korea / Sea of Japan)
GPS jamming over Korea
Unusual military air activity (Korea / Japan)
Internet disruption in South Korea
Mobilisation / reservist reports (Korea)
US nuclear command aircraft unusual
Spy-satellite passes converging on Korea
Forecast markets jump on Korea conflict

scenarios.name: Russia-NATO escalation
scenarios.sa_impact: Indirect: energy and market shock, cyber attacks that can spill over to Australian systems, and nuclear-risk rhetoric.
scenarios.why: Before February 2022: embassy departures, mobilisation reports, airspace closures and a surge in GPS jamming. Baltic and Black Sea jamming is now routine, so only spikes above normal count.

indicators.name: GPS jamming spike (Baltic / Black Sea)
Unusual military air activity (Eastern Europe)
Mobilisation / reservist reports (Russia / NATO)
Internet disruption in Russia
US nuclear command aircraft unusual
New US embassy departure order (Russia / Belarus / Ukraine region)
Private jets heading to retreat destinations
Market fear index above 30
Military blood supplies / field hospitals (Russia)
Russian signalling (Buzzer broadcasts, nuclear drills)
European defence stocks outperforming (5 days)
Russian wiper / Sandworm activity reports
Russian / Chinese vessels loitering over Baltic cables
Baltic undersea cable damage reported
Forecast markets jump on Russia-NATO conflict

scenarios.name: Nuclear use or alert
scenarios.sa_impact: Fallout risk to SA from a northern-hemisphere exchange is very low, but global trade, fuel and finance would be severely disrupted.
scenarios.why: Visible changes to US nuclear command aircraft (E-4B / E-6B), tanker surges, elite flight to remote retreats and market panic are the few public signals that would accompany a nuclear alert.

indicators.name: US nuclear command aircraft unusual
Air-refuelling tanker surge
Private jets heading to retreat destinations
Surge of long-range private jets
Market fear index above 35
Gold up 4%+ in a day
Mobilisation reports (any major power)
Forecast markets jump on nuclear use

scenarios.name: Australian infrastructure disruption
scenarios.sa_impact: Direct: loss of phone, internet, EFTPOS and fuel pumps. Cash, fuel and a pre-agreed meeting point matter most in the first 24 hours.
scenarios.why: The 2023 Optus outage cut mobile, NBN, EFTPOS and some 000 calls nationwide for 12 hours. Hostile states pre-position in critical infrastructure; GPS jamming over Australia would be a new and serious sign.

indicators.name: Phone / internet carrier outage
Two or more carriers down at once
GPS degradation over SA or NSW
New Australian cyber alert (ACSC)
ADF reserves called out
Mass casualty / Code Brown declared in Australia
Foreign vessel loitering over Australian cable corridors
Undersea cable damage reported (Australia / Pacific)
Ship traffic through Malacca / Sunda / Lombok down sharply
Sudden fall in SA electricity demand (possible large blackout)
Nationwide flight, power, network or payments halt in Australia

scenarios.name: Pandemic, biological or chemical emergency
scenarios.sa_impact: Health system strain, possible lockdowns and border closures, and shortages of medicines and protective equipment, which Australia mostly imports.
scenarios.why: Before COVID-19 (Dec 2019 - Feb 2020): reports of an unknown pneumonia cluster, WHO outbreak notices, mask and hazmat makers (Alpha Pro Tech, Lakeland) and vaccine developers (Moderna, Novavax) surging weeks before broad markets fell, and countries restricting exports of masks and medicines (Taiwan from 24 Jan 2020, then dozens more).

indicators.name: WHO outbreak report with a high-concern pathogen (last 14 days)
Unknown illness / pneumonia cluster reported
Countries restricting medical supply exports
Pandemic-response stocks outperforming (5 days)
Australian medicine or PPE shortage reports
Mass casualty declarations (any country)
Market fear index above 30
Chemical / nerve-agent attack or mass poisoning reported
Unexplained mass deaths or animal die-offs
Three or more Adelaide emergency departments 'very busy'

scenarios.name: Major cyber attack on Australia
scenarios.sa_impact: Banks, payments, hospitals, fuel distribution, telcos and the power grid all run on networks; a large attack can stop card payments and services for hours to days.
scenarios.why: Large attacks are usually preceded by quieter steps: a surge in newly exploited flaws in VPNs and firewalls (how state groups like Volt Typhoon get in), scanning of industrial-control systems, a rise in ransomware victims in the target country, and official warnings. Before Russia's 2022 invasion, wiper malware hit Ukraine a day ahead; Chinese groups have been found pre-positioned in US and allied infrastructure.

indicators.name: Global cyber threat level raised (SANS Infocon not green)
Surge in newly exploited vulnerabilities (2x normal week)
Several VPN / firewall flaws exploited this week
Spike in scanning of industrial-control systems
Australian ransomware victims above normal
New Australian cyber alert (ACSC)
Reports of state hackers / pre-positioning / wipers
Major Australian cyber incident reported
Phone / internet carrier outage
Sudden fall in SA electricity demand (possible large blackout)
Nationwide shutdown in an allied country (flights, power, networks, payments)

scenarios.name: AI-enabled attack (non-traditional)
scenarios.sa_impact: Not bombs but disruption: hacking at machine speed across banks, telcos, hospitals and the grid at once; fake videos or alerts from leaders causing panic buying or bank runs; or automated market and fraud shocks. Effects would be outages, payment failures and confusion about what is real.
scenarios.why: In November 2025 Anthropic reported the first documented AI-orchestrated cyber-espionage campaign: a Chinese state-sponsored group used an AI agent to carry out 80-90% of an attack on about 30 organisations, at thousands of requests per second. A fake AI image of a Pentagon explosion briefly moved US markets in May 2023, and a deepfake video call of a CFO tricked a company into paying US$25 million in 2024. The likely signature of an AI attack is breadth and speed: many unrelated systems and vendors hit at once, synthetic media of officials, and shocks with no clear human cause.

indicators.name: Exploited flaws across unusually many vendors at once
Reports of AI-driven hacking campaigns
Deepfakes of leaders or fake official alerts
Flash crash or exchange trading halt
Market fear index jumps 25%+ in a day
Major cloud or AI service outage
Phone / internet carrier outage
Surge in AI voice-clone / deepfake scams in Australia
Several VPN / firewall flaws exploited this week
Nationwide shutdown in an allied country, cause unknown
